name: Eastern Market
products: Produce, meat, eggs, flowers, specialty foods
notes: One of the largest historic public markets in the US and a main hub where regional farmers sell to Detroit.

name: Detroit Produce Terminal
notes: Wholesale terminal where produce from across North America is sold to grocers and restaurants.

name: Michigan Urban Farming Initiative
notes: Volunteer-run urban farm in Detroit's North End.

name: D-Town Farm
notes: Farm run by the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network.

name: Earthworks Urban Farm
notes: Urban farm run by the Capuchin Soup Kitchen.

name: Gleaners Community Food Bank
notes: Food bank that distributes food to pantries across Southeast Michigan.

name: Forgotten Harvest
notes: Rescues surplus food from grocers and restaurants and redistributes it.

name: Royal Oak Farmers Market
notes: Long-running covered farmers market in Oakland County.

name: Westview Orchards
notes: Family orchard and cider mill in northern Macomb County.

name: Blake Farms
notes: Orchard and cider mill in northern Macomb County.

name: Plymouth Orchards
notes: Orchard and cider mill in western Wayne County.

name: Wiard's Orchards
notes: Orchard and cider mill near Ypsilanti.

name: Calder Dairy
notes: Family dairy farm that bottles its own milk.

name: Guernsey Farms Dairy
notes: Local dairy known for milk and ice cream.

name: Leamington greenhouses
notes: One of the largest clusters of greenhouse vegetable farms in North America, about an hour from Detroit across the border.

name: The Thumb (Huron County)
products: Milk, dry beans, sugar beets, wheat
notes: One of Michigan's top farming counties.

name: Michigan Sugar country
notes: Sugar beets from mid-Michigan are processed into sugar.

name: Grand Traverse region
notes: Michigan grows most of the nation's tart cherries.

name: Fruit Ridge
notes: West Michigan's apple-growing heartland.

name: Southwest Michigan blueberries
notes: Michigan is one of the top blueberry-growing states.

name: Oceana County asparagus
notes: One of the country's main asparagus-growing areas.

name: Nogales port of entry
products: Tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, melons from Mexico
notes: A major crossing point for winter produce grown in Mexico.

name: Pharr port of entry
products: Avocados, limes, peppers and other produce from Mexico
notes: One of the busiest crossings for fresh produce coming from Mexico.

name: Salinas Valley
notes: Supplies much of the country's lettuce from spring through fall.

name: Yuma
notes: Takes over as the main lettuce source in winter.

name: California Central Valley
notes: One of the most productive farming regions in the world.

name: Southwest Florida
notes: A main winter source of fresh tomatoes for the eastern US.

name: Central America bananas
notes: Most bananas sold in the US come from Central and South America.

name: Wolverine Packing Co.
notes: Family-owned meat company that started as a lamb and veal packer in Eastern Market in 1937. Now in its fourth generation, it built a 180,000-square-foot plant in the district and ships across the US.

name: Kowalski Sausage
notes: Family-owned sausage maker that has made its products in Hamtramck for more than 100 years. Known for the giant neon kielbasa sign on its plant.

name: Dearborn Sausage Company
notes: Family-owned since Hungarian immigrant Victor Kosch founded it in 1946. Its products are sold in about 200 stores in Michigan, Ohio, Illinois and Canada.

name: Detroit Flight Path Farm
products: Heritage pork, chicken, duck, turkey, eggs
notes: Pasture-raised heritage pork and poultry a few miles south of Detroit Metro Airport, sold from a farm stand. Turkeys are ready for Thanksgiving and Christmas.

name: Judd Organic Angus Farms
notes: Beef cattle raised in the Carleton area of Monroe County and sold by online order.

name: Koegel Meats
notes: Family-owned Flint sausage maker known across Michigan for its Viennas.

name: Genuine Roots Farm
notes: Small pasture-based farm about an hour north of Detroit.

name: Michigan Turkey Producers
notes: Farmer-owned cooperative that processes turkeys raised on Michigan farms. It handled about 230 million pounds of live turkeys in 2023.

name: Clemens Food Group pork plant
notes: Large pork plant that opened in 2017 and can process about 10,000 hogs a day from farms in Michigan and nearby states. Before it opened, most Michigan hogs left the state to be processed.

name: Cass County hog farms
notes: One of a few Michigan counties where pigs outnumber people. Michigan raises about 2 million hogs a year.

name: Creswick Farms
notes: Farm raising animals without antibiotics or added hormones. It says many of its customers come from Detroit and Chicago.
